title: 实际线圈与电容并联的谐振
statement: 实际线圈（R = 80 Ω，L = 10 mH）与电容 C = 1 µF 并联，由正弦电流源 İ_s = 0.2∠0° A（有效值）供电，电源角频率等于电路的谐振角频率 ω₀（端口 a、0 之间阻抗为纯电阻）。
求谐振频率 f₀、谐振时的端口阻抗 Z₀ 和线圈电流 I₁ 的有效值。

questions.ask: 如果直接用 f = 1/(2π√(LC)) 计算谐振频率，会得到什么？
choices: 1591.5 Hz，偏大：线圈电阻较大时不能忽略 R²/L² 这一项
choiceExplain: 1/(2π√(LC)) = 1591.5 Hz，不是 954.9 Hz；两者只有在线圈电阻可以忽略（R ≪ √(L/C)）时才近似相等。
数值对了，方向反了：ω₀² = 1/(LC) − (R/L)²，减去一项后真实的 ω₀ 更小，所以 1/√(LC) 偏大。
只要 R < √(L/C) = 100 Ω，即 1/(LC) > (R/L)²，就存在谐振；R = 80 Ω 满足。没有谐振要 R ≥ √(L/C)。
questions.explain: 1/√(LC) = 10⁴ rad/s（1591.5 Hz）。实际线圈并联电容时，谐振条件是 ω₀C = ω₀L/(R² + ω₀²L²)，得 ω₀ = √(1/(LC) − (R/L)²) = 6000 rad/s。只有 R ≪ √(L/C)（高 Q 线圈）时，两者才近似相等；本题 R = 80 Ω 与 √(L/C) = 100 Ω 相当，差别很大。

hints: 并联电路用导纳：Y = jωC + 1/(R + jωL)，把线圈的导纳写成 G − jB 的形式。
1/(R + jωL) = (R − jωL)/(R² + ω²L²)；令虚部 ωC − ωL/(R² + ω²L²) = 0。
solution: **1. 导纳。** Y = jωC + (R − jωL)/(R² + ω²L²)。
**4. 各电流。** U = 0.2 × 125 = 25 V。İ₁ = 25/(80 + j60) = 0.2 − j0.15 A，有效值 **0.25 A**；İ_C = jω₀CU = j0.15 A。KCL：I₁ + I_C = 0.2 A = I_s ✓（线圈电流的无功分量被电容电流抵消）。

en.title: Resonance of a real coil in parallel with a capacitor
statement: A real coil (R = 80 Ω, L = 10 mH) is in parallel with a capacitor C = 1 µF, fed by a sinusoidal current source İ_s = 0.2∠0° A (rms) at the circuit's resonant angular frequency ω₀ (the impedance between a and 0 is purely resistive).
Find the resonant frequency f₀, the port impedance Z₀ at resonance and the rms coil current I₁.

questions.explain: At resonance Y = G_coil = R/(R² + ω₀²L²) = 80/(80² + 60²) = 80/10⁴ = 8 mS, so Z₀ = 1/Y = 125 Ω; it also equals L/(RC) = 0.01/(80 × 10⁻⁶) = 125 Ω.
U̇ = İ_s·Z₀ = 0.2 × 125 = 25 V and the coil impedance is 80 + j60 = 100∠36.87° Ω, so I₁ = 25/100 = 0.25 A — more than the source current.

questions.ask: What would you get by simply using f = 1/(2π√(LC))?
choices: 1591.5 Hz, too high: with a sizeable coil resistance the R²/L² term can't be ignored
choiceExplain: 1/(2π√(LC)) = 1591.5 Hz, not 954.9 Hz; the two agree only when the coil resistance is negligible (R ≪ √(L/C)).
Right number, wrong direction: ω₀² = 1/(LC) − (R/L)², so the true ω₀ is smaller and 1/√(LC) is too high.
Resonance exists as long as R < √(L/C) = 100 Ω, i.e. 1/(LC) > (R/L)²; R = 80 Ω satisfies it. There is no resonance only for R ≥ √(L/C).
questions.explain: 1/√(LC) = 10⁴ rad/s (1591.5 Hz). For a real coil in parallel with C the resonance condition is ω₀C = ω₀L/(R² + ω₀²L²), giving ω₀ = √(1/(LC) − (R/L)²) = 6000 rad/s. The two agree only when R ≪ √(L/C) (a high-Q coil); here R = 80 Ω is comparable to √(L/C) = 100 Ω, so the difference is large.

hints: Use admittance for the parallel circuit: Y = jωC + 1/(R + jωL), and write the coil's admittance as G − jB.
1/(R + jωL) = (R − jωL)/(R² + ω²L²); set the imaginary part ωC − ωL/(R² + ω²L²) to zero.
solution: **2. Resonance condition.** Zero imaginary part: C = L/(R² + ω₀²L²) → ω₀² = 1/(LC) − R²/L² = 10⁸ − (8000)² = 3.6×10⁷, ω₀ = **6000 rad/s**, f₀ ≈ **954.9 Hz**.
**3. Resonant impedance.** ω₀L = 60 Ω, Y = R/(R² + ω₀²L²) = 80/10000 = 8 mS, Z₀ = **125 Ω** (= L/(RC)).

**4. Currents.** U = 0.2 × 125 = 25 V. İ₁ = 25/(80 + j60) = 0.2 − j0.15 A, rms **0.25 A**; İ_C = jω₀CU = j0.15 A. KCL: I₁ + I_C = 0.2 A = I_s ✓ (the capacitor current cancels the reactive part of the coil current).
